SEB-301: machine view, a Human/Machine switch with a markdown twin of every page (#590)

Item 15 from the 21 Oct comment on SEB-301. No model is involved anywhere.

- tools/emit_markdown.py (new): renders each page headless the way a reader gets it and converts what it shows to markdown
  (headings, paragraphs, lists, tables -- including grid layouts the CSS lays out as rows, columns matched by position) --
  charts, pictures, the header and footer are left out. Writes index.md, countries.md, sending-money.md, sources.md,
  findings.md, how-it-works.md, how-it-was-built.md, one country/{CCY}.md per country and one finding/{id}.md per published
  finding, then llms.txt. Every number in a twin is checked against the page's own rendered text before anything is written;
  a page that renders nothing, or a twin that names no data file, fails loud and writes nothing.
- .github/workflows/collect.yml: one new step after the homepage bake, and the new files added to the commit (purely
  additive: a separate loop for the country/finding directories, nothing existing touched).
- js/machine_view.js + css/machine_view.css (new): a Human/Machine switch, bottom centre on every page with a twin.
  Machine shows the twin in a monospace panel with its path, size, an approximate token count, and three links (copy
  markdown, copy curl, open raw). Remembered per visitor in localStorage, inside try/catch. Every word in copy.json
  (machineView, empty slots: the writer fills them, same as every other reader-facing page).
- Each page's <head> gets <link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">, static on the seven top-level pages, set by a small
  inline script on country.html and finding.html since their twin depends on the query string.

Verified: every number in all 72 of this hour's twins was checked against the page's own rendered text (the emitter's own
check); re-checked by hand against 9 page types (home, countries, sending money, sources, findings, how it works, how it
was built, a country page, a finding page): 0 mismatches. Tested the switch in the browser on desktop and phone, Human and
Machine, with words filled in locally (copy.json ships with empty slots, so nothing shows until the writer fills them --
copy-lock, --style, --overflow, --lines and the design baseline all pass with the slots empty). Found and fixed a bug where
the switch could blank a page on first render before its content had finished building.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Roervig <sebastian.roervig@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

SEB-301: ignore iCloud duplicates of any extension and number (#587)

The old rule only covered "name N.ext" for one digit and five extensions, so 460 untracked copies such as "automerge 12.yml",
"actions-next 17.sh", "site_head 2.css" and "LOOPS_OFF 9" sat in the working tree where `git add -A` would stage them. A duplicate
workflow on main runs next to the real one (#578, 20 Oct). The rule now matches the same shape tools/check_junk_files.py fails a
PR for: one to three digits after a space, with or without an extension. No tracked file matches it.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Roervig <sebastian.roervig@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

SEB-301: one route list, read from collector.CORRIDORS (#586)

A route added to CORRIDORS in collector.py now reaches the Routes page with
no other edit. tools/routes_common.py derives the route list and each
route's panel file from collector.CORRIDORS and the route names from a new
copy.json block "routeNames" keyed by route. Every emitter that kept its own
copy (emit_routes, emit_corridor_summary, emit_providers, emit_latest,
emit_price_changes, emit_provider_receipts, audit_numbers, record_common,
and emit_record_daily's file list) reads it from there. js/route.js takes its
routes, and which are comparable, from data/routes_summary.json;
corridor.html's depth line takes them from data/corridor_summary.json.

tests/check_new_route.py adds a dummy route to a copy of CORRIDORS and finds
it in routes_summary.json.

SEB-301: route table entries merge themselves, done means data, and the builder can change collector.py (#583)

Item 0 of BACKLOG.md (21 Oct comment on SEB-301), rules (c) and (d), and what the route jobs need to be buildable:
- tools/check_additive.py: an existing collector may now get whole new entries in a route-keyed table it already has (CORRIDORS,
  CORRIDOR_CCY). No line removed or rewritten, the added lines are literal entries at the table's top level, keys are routes, and
  no key twice. The full collection run on the branch (collector-gate) still has to pass: same headers, every corridor that
  answered on main answers again. Tried on a real USD->PHP entry (passes) and a rewritten fee (refused).
- tools/backlog.py: a `rows:` line; a collection job gets `built: PR #N` instead of a tick and is not built again; `verify-data`
  ticks it when a row with that value and a later timestamp is on main, or blocks it with why after 2 hours.
- watchdog.yml: a backlog-data job runs verify-data every 30 minutes when a job is waiting, pushes BACKLOG.md and posts the result.
- tools/one_call.py: a file over 40,000 characters is sent in the parts the job names (`excerpt:` lines) and changed by
  find-and-replace edits; a collection job without a `rows:` line is blocked; a changed collector's own --selftest runs.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Roervig <sebastian.roervig@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

SEB-302: the flip-hold test picks a country whose latest hour is normal (#582)

The test took the first single-board person-to-person country, which since 23:40 UTC on 20 Oct is Sudan. Sudan's own number has
been far above its 7-day level for more than 3 hours in a row (2,188% to 2,208% against a median near 1,700%), so the rule confirms
a further move by time and a bad row is published, as the rule says. The number is right; the test's pick was wrong. It now skips a
country whose latest published hour is already outside its usual range. Today it tests Mozambique and passes. This check was red on
every main push and blocked every PR.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Roervig <sebastian.roervig@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
